answer.rationale: The security patch cannot be reverted (eliminates rollback_release and any release-gating memory relevance). p99 latency is climbing on the write path while settlement traffic is at peak. Proven patterns from memory show that provisioning headroom before load absorbed surge (b3), and routing reads off the primary recovered write latency the same day (b5). I want to verify b3 because it directly evidences that adding capacity headroom before peak absorbed surge and kept queue depth flat — the most direct analogue to the current situation. With only one intervention slot, I choose add_capacity as the single action that maximizes sustained availability without losing writes: it is non-revertive, compatible with the security patch, addresses the proximate cause (write-path saturation during peak), and aligns with a verified historical success.
